title: BrainWorld: Modeling Whole-Brain Functional Dynamics through Predictive 4D fMRI Generation
claim: Prior models use separate encoders with task and modality-role mismatch and no controllable generation; ours conditions generation on a structural prior.
layout: 2 panels, left prior and right ours, imagination analogy cartoon top-right
description: Two panels. Panel (a), on the left, shows existing approaches. A 4D fMRI brain sequence (t0 to t2) goes through an encoder to a green feature vector, and that goes to downstream tasks. Another path feeds a 3D MRI through its own encoder to a blue feature vector. Both paths merge in a 'Parallel modality fusion' box. Orange-red X marks label the flaws: lack of controllable generation, task mismatch, no structural prior, and modality-role mismatch. Panel (b), on the right, starts with a head silhouette thinking 'Apple'. A noisy apple sharpens over time next to wavy time-series traces, which is the imagination analogy. A dotted double arrow links this to the BrainWorld pipeline below. In that pipeline, fMRI goes through a VAE encoder to a DiT, with the 3D MRI encoder supplying a structural prior. A VAE decoder then outputs future frames t3 to t5, and a feature aggregator feeds downstream tasks. Green checkmarks mark the benefits.
caption: Motivation. Inspired by the process of imagination, BrainWorld addresses the task and modality-fusion mismatches by using sMRI as a conditioning input, guiding the generation of fMRI. As the brain refines vague concepts (e.g., an apple) into detailed features, BrainWorld leverages sMRI to transform the initial vague state into accurate predictions, naturally facilitating modality fusion for downstream tasks.
abstract: Whole-brain four-dimensional functional magnetic resonance imaging (4D fMRI) generation is valuable for modeling functional brain dynamics, yet existing fMRI foundation models mainly target representation learning and downstream prediction rather than conditional predictive generation. We introduce BrainWorld, a structural-prior-conditioned generative model for whole-brain 4D fMRI dynamics. BrainWorld uses structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) as subject-level anatomical context and past functional connectivity as recent dynamic context to guide future fMRI generation, integrating both structural and functional condi- tions into the denoising process. Using 22 datasets for model development and evaluation, BrainWorld supports autoregressive generation of up to 400 frames, improves downstream performance through generated-example augmentation, and learns transferable multimodal representations that outperform baselines. Together, these results establish BrainWorld as a condition-aware generative framework for long-horizon brain dynamics modeling and multimodal representation learning.
